scenes.title: Truth in the Courtyard
scenes.summary: M3 explains how he accidentally swapped suitcases with F3 on Monday's train and panicked at the gate.
scenes.intro: Still standing under the courtyard tree at the {SHOW} in {CITY}, {M3} sits down with {F1} and {F3} to explain Monday night's mystery from the very beginning. Listen first.
story: Let me look at you properly, {M3}! You grew taller than the piano!
I cannot believe you are staying in the exact same guesthouse, Madam {F3}.
Wait—so we rode the same train on Monday, and you took her suitcase?
By complete accident! At my cousin's flat I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.
Why did you leave my bag on the step at night and run away?
Because when I walked here on Monday evening, I saw my older brother walking down this street!
Your older brother lives here in {CITY}?
Yes. I panicked, rang your bell, and slipped the Friday note onto the handle.
Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?
I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly forgot you still had my bag!
Until you called us on Tuesday asking us not to open the white parcel!
Everything in that white paper belongs to my brother {M4}, not me.
scenes.outro: All the puzzle pieces from Monday and Tuesday finally click together! Next time, {M3} explains why he has not spoken to his brother {M4} in three years.

scenes.title: Three Years of Silence
scenes.summary: At the front desk M1 unlocks the blue suitcase for M3, who explains the three-year silence with his brother M4.
scenes.intro: Inside at the front desk, {M1} brings the dark-blue suitcase out of the closet for {M3} and {F1}. Now it is Friday morning, three hours before noon. Listen first.
story: So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping upstairs under my attic roof all along.
Sorry for the trouble, {M1}. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.
Why could you not simply hand {M4} the wooden train at his front door?
Three years ago, after our grandfather died, {M4} and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.
Family houses and old memories—those arguments cut deep.
We have not spoken since that Sunday. Last week I sent him one short postcard.
Asking him to meet you here on Friday at noon?
Actually, I only wrote: 'Something from Grandfather is waiting at the {SHOW} Friday at noon.'
Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, stubborn big brother would stay home!
Wait—you were planning to hand the clerk the bag and watch from across the street?!
That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.
scenes.outro: Instead of hiding across the street, {M3} has three hours to find the courage to stay right here in the courtyard. See you next time.

scenes.title: Friday Lemon Cake
scenes.summary: F3 recalls what the brothers always ate after Friday piano lessons, giving F2 a bright baking idea.
scenes.intro: At nine thirty in the café corner, {F2} pours fresh coffee for {F3} and {M3} as they reminisce about Friday afternoons twenty-five years ago. Listen first.
story: So, {M3}, you are really staying in the courtyard to greet {M4} at noon?
Yes, {F2}. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.
{M4} will not walk out. He always acted tough for five seconds, then softened.
You still remember that after all these years?
Of course! Every Friday when he missed a piano note, he frowned at the wall.
How did you get him smiling again, Madam {F3}?
His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with powdered sugar on top!
Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—we fought over the corner piece every single Friday!
Hold everything! What time is it right now? Nine thirty-five!
{F2}, please do not go to extra work because of us.
Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now—this kitchen was waiting for today!
Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!
scenes.outro: Six fresh lemons in the kitchen basket and two hours until noon—{F2} is already tying on her apron! Let's step out into the courtyard next time.

scenes.title: Two Chairs Under the Tree
scenes.summary: F1, F2, and M1 arrange a quiet corner table under the courtyard tree and check the string of lanterns.
scenes.intro: At eleven o'clock, the sweet smell of baking lemon cake drifts into the courtyard while {F1}, {F2}, and {M1} prepare a small round table under the shade tree. Listen first.
story: Let us put the small wooden table right here under the tree, away from the door.
Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs instead of the lobby window.
Here is a clean white cloth and two blue teacups.
{M1}, are you polishing those hanging paper lanterns for noon?
The wire needed straightening anyway. Nothing sentimental about good maintenance.
Oh, listen to Mr Maintenance! Yesterday you fixed the boiler, today you fix two brothers!
I fix pipes and chairs. People have to fix their own words.
What time does your watch say now, {M1}?
Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust and sweet lemon sugar!
Look upstairs at the attic window: {M3} has changed his shirt three times!
Go talk to him, {F1}, before he wears out the floorboards!
scenes.outro: Two chairs under the tree, warm lemon cake cooling on the rack, and forty minutes left on the clock. Next time, {F1} helps {M3} find the right first words.

scenes.title: Simple Words First
scenes.summary: At eleven forty M3 practices stiff speeches in the courtyard until F1 helps him choose three simple, honest lines.
scenes.intro: Twenty minutes before noon, {M3} paces across the courtyard stones holding a crumpled sheet of notes while {F1} walks over with a glass of water. Listen first.
story: Here, drink a sip of cool water, {M3}. What is on that paper?
A five-minute speech explaining nineteen reasons why we were both wrong in April.
Nineteen reasons?! Are you welcoming your brother or reading a railway timetable?
When I get nervous, my sentences grow very long and formal!
Fold that paper and put it in your pocket right now.
Without my notes, what do I say when he walks through that gate?
Start with three short sentences. First: 'Hello, {M4}, thank you for coming.'
'Hello, {M4}, thank you for coming.' Okay, I can remember that.
Second: 'I missed you these three years.'
'I missed you these three years.' Honest and clear. And third?
'Sit down—there is hot tea and Friday lemon cake.'
Tea and lemon cake! {F1}, you should open a school for nervous brothers.
scenes.outro: No nineteen-point speech—just 'thank you for coming', 'I missed you', and 'sit down for tea and lemon cake'. Ten minutes left until noon! See you next time.

scenes.title: Ten Minutes to Twelve
scenes.summary: At eleven fifty the postman drops off an official registered letter for M2, who sets it aside to greet noon.
scenes.intro: Inside at the front desk at eleven fifty, {M2} straightens his clean blue tie while {F1} and {F2} check the clock—just as the morning postman leaves a thick white envelope on the counter. Listen first.
story: How does my tie look today, {F1}? Zero orange juice in sight!
Sharp and spotless, {M2}! Even your glasses are on your nose instead of your forehead.
Progress! Today our courtyard hosts a family reunion—quiet dignity from everyone!
Says the man peeking through the lace curtain every thirty seconds!
I am checking the weather, {F2}! Who left this thick envelope by the bell?
The postman just asked me to sign for it. It has a red property-office stamp.
From the building landlord's lawyer? Strange—our rent is paid until next summer.
Open it after twelve, boss! Look at the clock: five minutes to noon!
Right you are. Paperwork can wait—put it beside the ledger for now.
I placed the blue suitcase right beside {M3}'s table under the tree.
And the teapot is hot! Everybody step back from the window!
Listen... the church clock down the street is starting to chime twelve!
scenes.outro: That thick envelope with the red property stamp sits unopened on the desk as the church bells begin to strike twelve! Let's step out to the gate next time.

scenes.title: Twelve Chimes
scenes.summary: Twelve o'clock strikes with an empty gate, M3 loses hope for a long minute, and then a taxi brakes outside.
scenes.intro: Out in the courtyard, the twelfth bell fades into the midday air over {CITY}. {M3} stands beside the blue suitcase while {F1} and {M1} wait near the doorway. Listen first.
story: Twelve chimes... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.
Give it a few minutes, {M3}. City traffic at noon is always slow.
And big brothers never arrive early when they want to look calm.
Look, it is twelve-oh-four already. Maybe he threw my postcard in the bin.
Do not sit down defeated yet! Keep looking toward the corner.
Three years was too long to wait, {F1}. I should have called him two winters ago.
Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?
A yellow taxi just pulled up outside the iron gate!
My hands are shaking—is there a tall man in a dark grey coat?
Tall, dark grey coat, looking up at our guesthouse sign right now!
There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.
Shoulders back, {M3}. Remember your three simple sentences—I will open the gate!
scenes.outro: At four minutes past noon, a tall man in a dark grey coat rings the courtyard bell! One final scene in Episode 5—back inside at the front desk, {M2} opens that letter. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Red-Stamped Letter
scenes.summary: As M4 steps into the courtyard outside, M2 opens the landlord's letter inside and turns pale at a sale notice.
scenes.intro: After letting {M4} into the courtyard to give the brothers privacy, {F1} slips quietly back inside to the front desk, where {F2} watches warmly and {M2} slits open the registered envelope. Listen first.
story: {F1}, look through the glass—they are standing face to face under the tree!
Neither of them walked away! {M3} is pointing at the two chairs right now!
Wonderful... let me just glance at this landlord letter while we wait.
Probably a boring notice about painting the street shutters.
Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My knees feel weak.
{M2}! Your face went completely white! Sit down—what does the letter say?
Read the top line for me, {F1}. Tell me my glasses are playing tricks again!
'Notice of Property Transfer: Number Eight Courtyard Building offered for commercial office sale.'
Commercial office sale?! Turn our guesthouse and kitchen into grey offices?!
They give us thirty days before new buyers inspect the building!
Wait—there is a second folded page clipped to the back of this notice...
Not a word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!
scenes.outro: Outside under the tree two estranged brothers are finally sitting down together—while inside at the desk, a thirty-day commercial sale notice threatens the entire {SHOW}! Episode 5 is done; join us for the Season 1 finale in Episode 6.
